jobs.occupation: Head of Structures (all genders) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLEWe are looking for an experienced and passionate Head of Structures to lead and further develop our growing structures team.In this role, you will take overall technicalresponsibility for the structural development of our VTOL aircrafts, fro initial concepts and structural architecture through detailed design, analysis, manufacturing support and structural testing.You will define the structural strategy, make key technical decisions and ensure that lightweight, robust, manufacturable and certifiable structures are developed inline with the overall aircraft and programme objectives. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of structural design and analysis engineers while remaining closely involved in design reviews, prototype manufacturing, aircraft integration and structural testing.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
• You lead and further develop the structures team and take overall technical responsibility for the aircraft structure, from preliminary design through detailed design, manufacturing, testing and flight operations
• You define and maintain the structural architecture, load paths, design principles and material concepts and lead the development of primary and secondary structures, including fuselage, wings, empennage, propulsion-supporting structures, landing gear interfaces and system installations
• You define structural requirements, verification methods, test strategies and acceptance criteria and coordinate analyses covering strength, stiffness, stability, fatigue, damage tolerance, vibration and dynamic behaviour
• You plan, review and support coupon, component, subassembly and full-scale structural tests and ensure compliance with applicable airworthiness requirements, certification objectives and internal development processes
• You coordinate closely with Loads, Flight Physics, Systems Engineering, Manufacturing, Testing, Certification and Quality to develop lightweight, robust, manufacturable and integrated structural solutions.
• You review and approve structural concepts, calculations, drawings, reports and test documentation and manage structural risks, deviations, design changes and corrective actions
• You actively support prototype manufacturing, structural assembly, aircraft integration, ground and flight testing and the resolution of practical issues, structural findings, damage or failures directly on the hardware
• You establish and continuously improve engineering processes, methods, tools and documentation standards and support the selection and coordination of external development and manufacturing partners
• You translate the structural development roadmap into clear priorities and responsibilities and support the growth of the team through recruiting, onboarding, mentoring and technical development

WHAT YOU BRING
• You hold an academic degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering or a comparable technical course of study
• Several years of professional experience in aircraft structures, including responsibility for structural design, analysis or verification, form part of your background
• Strong experience in the development of lightweight aircraft structures from initial concept through detailed design and testing is something you bring to the table
• You have extensive knowledge of composite, metallic and sandwich structures, including relevant manufacturing and joining technologies
• Structural mechanics, load paths, finite element analysis, strength, stability, fatigue and structural testing form part of your technical expertise
• You bring strong hands-on experience in the manufacturing, assembly, modification, repair or testing of aircraft structures and prototypes
• You are comfortable working directly with prototypes and hardware and enjoy resolving practical structural and integration challenges together with the workshop and test teams
• Leading a multidisciplinary engineering team while remaining technically and practically involved is something you are capable of
• You are able to make technical decisions and balance weight, performance, safety, manufacturability, cost and schedule
• Target-oriented self-management comes naturally to you, along with a structured and pragmatic working style
• Strong problem-solving, communication, leadership and technical writing skills complete your profile.
• Fluent English rounds out your qualifications

The following would further strengthen your application:
• Experience with the structural development of VTOL aircraft, helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, UAVs or other lightweight aerospace systems is a plus
• Knowledge of EASA regulations and guidance material for UAS and eVTOL development, such as SORA, SC Light-UAS or SC-VTOL, is a valuable asset
• Experience with structural compliance demonstration, certification documentation and coordination with certification authorities adds to your profile
• Familiarity with finite element and design tools such as ANSYS, Nastran, Abaqus, Siemens NX or comparable software strengthens your application
• Experience with composite manufacturing processes, bonded joints and mechanically fastened joints is an advantage
• Planning and conducting structural test campaigns, from test definition and readiness through execution and data evaluation, is something you have done before
• Experience in building up or growing an engineering team, including hiring and mentoring, rounds out your qualifications
• German language skills are an advantage

WHAT WE OFFER
• Full-scale aerospace engineering, not concept slides
• A 60+ engineer team at Ottobrunn
• Real ownership and flat hierarchies: a modern startup culture where your input shapes decisions, not just execution
• Flexible working hours, remote work, and competitive compensation
• Health & wellbeing: EGYM Wellpass membership and subsidized lunch in our canteen
• Office extras: espresso coffee, fresh fruit, and soft drinks, plus regular team and company ev

You will drive and execute regional quality and regulatory strategies, translating requirements into practical business actions that enable market access, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth.

Translate regulatory requirements into clear business implications and actionable guidance for leadership teams.- Act as key interface to health authorities and external stakeholders, representing the organization with credibility and impact.

**3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d) **

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following two positions in the Department of Palaeontology & Historical Geology and the Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as of 01 January 2027

3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d)

(full time / part time)

Location: Frankfurt (Hesse)

Organizational units:

Department of Palaeontology & Historlcal Geology, Section Amber Research

Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology, Section Palaeomammalogy

Department of Palaeoanthropology, Section Mammalogy

Employment scope: Full-time / Part-time

Type of contract: Project-based, fixed-term for three years

Remuneration: Collective agreement of Hesse, TV-H E 9

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.

Within the framework of the project "SCRE3NED: Senckenberg Collection's RarEst – 3-dimensioNal Enhanced Digitisation", type specimens of exceptional scientific value (holotypes, paratypes and lectotypes) from various collections of the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt (amber, extant and fossil mammals, Messel fossils) are digitised using micro-computed tomography (μCT), synchrotron radiation-based micro-computed tomography (SRμCT), and digital photography. The aim is to produce high-quality, standardised and FAIR-compliant 2D and 3D datasets for research, collection management and science communication.

Your tasks

- Performing and documenting μCT scans in accordance with established quality standards
- Supporting the preparation and execution of SRμCT scanning campaigns at external research facilities
- Reconstruction, segmentation and quality control of 3D image datasets
- Contributing to the implementation of photography-based digitisation methods
- Creation, maintenance and management of metadata in accordance with the FAIR principles
- Preparation and integration of digital datasets into the collection databases (DINA, SeSam/AQUiLA)
- Further development, optimisation and standardisation of workflows for the 3D digitisation of a range of different object groups
- Ensuring consistent data and file organisation as well as long-term archiving
- Collaboration with curators, scientists, IT specialists and external project partners

Your profile

- Completed vocational training in a technical or scientific field (e.g., technical assistant for natural history museums and research institutes, biological or medical laboratory technician, photographic technical assistant, preparator) or a completed university degree (Bachelor's/Master's) in biology, earth sciences, medical engineering, computer science, engineering, media technology or a related field, or a comparable qualification with relevant professional experience
- Practical experience with imaging techniques, preferably computed tomography
- Confident use of software for 3D image processing and segmentation (e.g., Avizo/Amira, VGStudio MAX, Dragonfly, 3D Slicer).
- Good IT skills and a willingness to familiarise yourself with new software environments
- Knowledge of digital data management and data organisation
- Careful and responsible handling of unique and sometimes fragile objects
- Valid category B driving licence
- A structured, independent and solution-oriented approach to work, combined with the ability to work well in a team
- Good written and spoken German and English

Desirable skills

- Experience in operating and working with computed tomography systems
- Knowledge of 3D printing techniques and of preparing models for printing
- Experience with photography-based digitisation methods, in particular photogrammetry
- Familiarity with the FAIR principles and experience with repositories for 3D data (e.g., MorphoSource) or with collection databases
- Interest in natural history collections, biodiversity research and digitisation
- Basic knowledge of vertebrate and insect morphology

We offer

- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please submit your application electronically as a single PDF file, including a cover letter, CV, and relevant certificates and references by 04.10.2026.

If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our career page (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/stellenanzeigen/ ) and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.
